q21157.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, passing is forbidden.

explain.short: Arms open towards you mean the same as a red light, so you cannot pass.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'è vietato il passaggio' (passing is forbidden) is exactly what a red light means.

sceneParams.caption: Arms open towards you: you may not pass
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21158.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, you must stop before the stop line.

explain.short: This position is like a red light, and at a red light you stop before the stop line.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'prima della striscia' (before the line) is correct: you never stop on or after it.

sceneParams.caption: Stop before the stop line
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21159.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, you cannot turn left.

explain.short: Arms open towards you stop all movement, so turning left is not allowed either.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'non si può svoltare a sinistra' is true because ALL directions are closed.

sceneParams.caption: No left turn: everything is closed
lines: = red light: stop at the line

keywords.it: non si può svoltare a sinistra

q21160.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, you cannot cross the junction.

explain.short: This signal is like red, so you must wait and not cross the junction (incrocio).
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'non si può attraversare l'incrocio' is correct: you stop before it.

sceneParams.caption: You may not cross the junction
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21161.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, you cannot turn right.

explain.short: Arms open towards you stop every direction, the right turn too.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'non si può svoltare a destra' is true: there is no free right turn here.

sceneParams.caption: No right turn either
lines: = red light: stop at the line

keywords.it: non si può svoltare a destra

q21162.en: The officer's position with arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, is the same as the red traffic light.

explain.short: Arms open towards you (front or back) have the same meaning as a red light: stop.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'equivale alla luce rossa' (is the same as red) is the key fact to remember.

sceneParams.caption: Arms open towards you = red light
lines: = red light: stop at the line

keywords.en: is the same as the red light

q21163.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, you may go if you turn right, but you must give way to pedestrians crossing.

explain.short: This signal is like red for every direction, so you may not turn right either.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'si può passare se si svolta a destra' is the trap: there is no free right turn.

sceneParams.caption: Right turn is NOT allowed: wait
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21164.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards the direction the driver comes from, as in the picture, the driver may go on, but with great care and at moderate speed.

explain.short: Arms open towards the driver are like a red light: the driver must stop, not go on.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'questi può procedere' (he may go on) is wrong: 'massima prudenza' does not change a red.

sceneParams.caption: The driver must stop, not go on slowly
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21165.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, you must sound the horn, but moderately, to get the officer's attention.

explain.short: You simply stop and wait; honking at the officer is useless and not required.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'bisogna suonare il clacson' (you must honk) is invented: the rule says stop.

sceneParams.caption: Stop and wait, no horn
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21166.en: When the officer stands with his arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, you may turn, but not go straight on.

explain.short: Arms open towards you close ALL directions: no turning and no going straight.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'si può svoltare' (you may turn) is wrong: turns are forbidden too.

sceneParams.caption: No turns and no straight on
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21167.en: The officer's position with arms open towards our direction, as in the picture, is the same as the green traffic light.

explain.short: Arms open towards you mean red, not green.
explain.rule: A traffic officer (vigile) facing you, from the front or from the back, with arms open is like a red light. You must stop before the stop line and you may not go straight or turn.
explain.trap: 'luce verde' (green light) is the trap: the correct colour is red.

sceneParams.caption: Arms open towards you = RED, not green
lines: = red light: stop at the line

q21168.en: When the officer stands side-on with his arms open, as in the picture, the traffic flows moving parallel to his arms are allowed to pass.

explain.short: Side-on with arms open gives green to the traffic that moves along the line of his arms.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'parallele alle sue braccia' (parallel to his arms) tells you WHO may pass.

sceneParams.caption: Traffic parallel to his arms may pass
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21169.en: When the officer stands side-on with his arms open, as in the picture, you may turn right if you come from his right or from his left.

explain.short: Vehicles from his right or left have green, and green allows turning right too.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua destra o dalla sua sinistra' are exactly the sides parallel to his arms.

sceneParams.caption: From his right or left: you may turn right
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21170.en: When the officer stands side-on with his arms open, as in the picture, the traffic flows moving parallel to his arms may cross the junction, but with care.

explain.short: Traffic parallel to his arms has green, and at green you cross carefully.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'ma usando prudenza' (but with care) is normal at any green, so it does not make it false.

sceneParams.caption: Parallel traffic crosses, with care
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21171.en: The officer's side-on position with arms open, as in the picture, is the same as the green traffic light for the traffic flows moving parallel to his arms.

explain.short: For traffic along his arms, this position means green.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'luce verde' is right here, but only for traffic 'parallele alle sue braccia'.

sceneParams.caption: Parallel to his arms = green light
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21172.en: When the officer stands side-on with his arms open, as in the picture, you must go straight on.

explain.short: This position works like green: you may go straight or turn, nobody forces you straight.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'obbligatoriamente' (compulsorily) is the trap: green does not force one direction.

sceneParams.caption: Green: straight OR turn, your choice
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21173.en: When the officer stands side-on with his arms open, as in the picture, you must stop before the stop line if you come from his left.

explain.short: Coming from his left you are parallel to his arms, so you have green and do not stop.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua sinistra' is a side parallel to his arms: there you go, you do not stop.

sceneParams.caption: From his left: green, no stop
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21174.en: When the officer stands side-on with his arms open, as in the picture, you must stop after passing the pedestrian crossing stripes.

explain.short: Nobody stops after the zebra crossing: parallel traffic goes, and the others stop BEFORE the line.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'dopo aver superato' (after passing) is wrong: stopping on the far side is never right.

sceneParams.caption: Never stop after the zebra crossing
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21175.en: The officer's side-on position with arms open, as in the picture, is the same as the red traffic light for the traffic flows moving parallel to his arms.

explain.short: For traffic parallel to his arms this position means green, not red.
explain.rule: When the officer stands side-on (di profilo) with arms open, traffic moving parallel to his arms (coming from his right or his left) has green: it may go straight or turn, with care. Traffic coming from his front or back must stop.
explain.trap: 'luce rossa' is the trap: red is for traffic facing his chest or back.

sceneParams.caption: Parallel to his arms = green, not red
lines: From his front or back: stop

q21176.en: The officer's position with one arm raised, as in the picture, is the same as the steady yellow traffic light.

explain.short: One raised arm has the same meaning as a steady yellow light.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'gialla fissa' (steady yellow) is correct: not red, not flashing.

sceneParams.caption: One arm raised = steady yellow
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21177.en: If the officer has one arm raised, as in the picture, you must quickly clear the junction if you have already entered it.

explain.short: Like with yellow: if you are already in the junction, you leave it quickly.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'se già è stato impegnato' (if already entered) is the key condition.

sceneParams.caption: Already in the junction: clear it fast
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21178.en: If the officer has one arm raised, as in the picture, you must stop before the junction if you can do it without causing danger.

explain.short: Like with yellow, you stop before the junction, but only if stopping is safe.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'senza creare pericolo' (without causing danger) is the yellow-light condition.

sceneParams.caption: Stop before the junction, if safe
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21179.en: The officer's position with one arm raised, as in the picture, is a signal only for vehicles that have to turn.

explain.short: The raised arm is like yellow for ALL vehicles, not only for those turning.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'riservata solo' (only for) is the trap: it is for everybody.

sceneParams.caption: For ALL vehicles, not only turners
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21180.en: If the officer has one arm raised, as in the picture, you must stop in every case.

explain.short: Like yellow, you stop only if it is safe; if you are already in the junction you clear it.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in every case) is the trap: yellow allows exceptions.

sceneParams.caption: Not 'in every case': only if safe
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21181.en: If the officer has one arm raised, as in the picture, you are only allowed to turn right.

explain.short: A raised arm is like yellow: it is about stopping, not about one allowed direction.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'soltanto svoltare a destra' (only turn right) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: It means yellow, not 'right turn only'
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21182.en: If the officer has one arm raised, as in the picture, you must slow down only if there are tram tracks in the junction.

explain.short: A raised arm is like yellow at every junction, with or without tram tracks.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'solo se ... binari del tram' (only if tram tracks) is the trap: trams do not matter.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow everywhere, tram tracks or not
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21183.en: The officer's position with the arm raised, as in the picture, is the same as the red traffic light.

explain.short: A raised arm means yellow, not red. Red is arms open towards you.
explain.rule: An officer with one arm raised is like a steady yellow light, for everybody. Stop before the junction if you can do it safely; if you are already in the junction, clear it quickly.
explain.trap: 'luce rossa' is the trap: the right colour is steady yellow.

sceneParams.caption: Arm raised = yellow, not red
lines: Stop if you can do it safely

q21184.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, allows vehicles coming from his left to turn left.

explain.short: Vehicles from his left are the only ones free to move, in any direction, left included.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua sinistra' (from his left) is the side that may go.

sceneParams.caption: From his left: left turn allowed
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21185.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, stops vehicles coming from his right.

explain.short: Only traffic from his left may move, so traffic from his right is stopped.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua destra' (from his right) is a stopped side: only his left goes.

sceneParams.caption: From his right: stop
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21186.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, forbids vehicles coming from behind him to go straight on.

explain.short: Vehicles from behind him are not the ones from his left, so they must stop and cannot go straight.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalle sue spalle' (from his back) is a stopped side.

sceneParams.caption: From behind him: no straight on
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21187.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, allows vehicles coming from his left to go straight on.

explain.short: Traffic from his left has green, so going straight is allowed.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua sinistra' is the free side: straight on is fine.

sceneParams.caption: From his left: straight on allowed
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21188.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, allows vehicles coming from his left to turn right.

explain.short: Traffic from his left may go in every direction, right included.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua sinistra' is the free side: right turn is fine.

sceneParams.caption: From his left: right turn allowed
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21189.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, allows vehicles coming from his right to turn right.

explain.short: Vehicles from his right are stopped, so they cannot turn right either.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua destra' (from his right) is the trap: that side must stop.

sceneParams.caption: From his right: stop, no turning
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21190.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, allows vehicles coming from behind him to turn right.

explain.short: Vehicles from behind him must stop; only those from his left may move.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalle sue spalle' (from behind him) is the trap: that side waits.

sceneParams.caption: From behind him: stop
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21191.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, allows vehicles coming from his right to turn left.

explain.short: Vehicles from his right are stopped, so no left turn for them.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua destra' is the trap: only 'sua sinistra' may move.

sceneParams.caption: From his right: no left turn
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21192.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, allows vehicles coming from his right to go straight on.

explain.short: Vehicles from his right are stopped; going straight is for those from his left.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'dalla sua destra' is the trap: right and left are swapped.

sceneParams.caption: From his right: stop, no straight on
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21193.en: The officer standing with arms at a right angle, as in the picture, forbids passing to vehicles coming from his left.

explain.short: Vehicles from his left are exactly the ones allowed to pass.
explain.rule: With the officer's arms at a right angle as in the picture, only vehicles coming from his LEFT may move: straight on, right or left. Vehicles coming from his right or from behind him must stop.
explain.trap: 'vieta il passaggio' is wrong for 'dalla sua sinistra': that is the free side.

sceneParams.caption: From his left you MAY pass
lines: From his LEFT: go any way
From his right or back: stop

q21194.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer means that all vehicles must stop, in safe conditions.

explain.short: A long whistle is the officer's signal for everybody to stop, but safely.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'tutti i veicoli' (all vehicles) is correct: nobody is excluded.

sceneParams.caption: Long whistle: everybody stops safely
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

keywords.it: tutti i veicoli si devono arrestare

q21195.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer is used to let emergency vehicles on duty pass.

explain.short: The officer stops all traffic with a long whistle so that ambulances or fire engines can get through.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'veicoli di soccorso' (emergency vehicles) is the typical reason for the long whistle.

sceneParams.caption: Stops traffic for emergency vehicles
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

q21196.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer requires those who have entered the junction to clear it and, if needed, to stop just after it.

explain.short: If you are already in the junction you must not stay there: clear it, then stop.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'liberarlo' (clear it) is right: you never block the junction.

sceneParams.caption: Already inside: clear it, then stop
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

q21197.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer means you must stop, if you have not yet entered the junction.

explain.short: Before the junction, a long whistle means you stop and wait.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'se non si è ancora occupato l'incrocio' (not yet in the junction) is the case where you stop.

sceneParams.caption: Not in the junction yet: stop
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

q21198.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer means you must turn back.

explain.short: A long whistle means stop, not turn back.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'tornare indietro' (turn back) is invented: you just stop.

sceneParams.caption: Stop, do not turn back
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

q21199.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer is used to stop or divert only vehicles coming from his right.

explain.short: The long whistle stops ALL vehicles, from every direction.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'solo ... dalla sua destra' (only from his right) is the trap: it is for everybody.

sceneParams.caption: All directions stop, not only his right
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

q21200.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer means that stopped vehicles must start moving.

explain.short: The long whistle means stop, the opposite of starting to move.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'mettersi in marcia' (start moving) is the opposite of the real meaning.

sceneParams.caption: It means stop, not start moving
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

q21201.en: The long whistle blast from the traffic officer requires only heavy vehicles to stop.

explain.short: The long whistle is for all vehicles, cars included.
explain.rule: A long whistle blast from the traffic officer means ALL vehicles must stop, safely, usually to let emergency vehicles through. If you are already in the junction, clear it and then stop just after it.
explain.trap: 'ai soli veicoli pesanti' (only heavy vehicles) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: All vehicles stop, not only trucks
lines: Not in the junction yet: stop

q21202.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you must stop at the stop line.

explain.short: Red lights mean a train is coming; the barrier will drop soon, so you stop at the line.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'semibarriera ancora alzata' (barrier still up) does not matter: red means stop.

sceneParams.caption: Red lights: stop at the stop line

q21203.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you must not speed up to cross before the half-barrier comes down.

explain.short: Racing the barrier is very dangerous: the train is already on its way.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'non si deve accelerare' (you must not speed up) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Never race the barrier

q21204.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you may pass quickly if you cannot see a train coming.

explain.short: Red lights mean stop, whether or not you can see the train.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'se non si vede' (if you cannot see) is the trap: trains are fast and may be hidden.

sceneParams.caption: No train in sight? Still stop

q21205.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you must speed up to clear the crossing quickly.

explain.short: With red lights on you stop before the crossing, you do not speed up.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'bisogna accelerare' (you must speed up) is the opposite of the rule.

sceneParams.caption: Do not speed up: stop

q21206.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you must stop at the third distance panel.

explain.short: You stop at the stop line near the barrier, not at the distance panels before it.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'terzo pannello distanziometrico' (third distance panel) is the wrong place: panels only warn.

sceneParams.caption: Stop at the stop line, not at a panel

q21207.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you may cross if the railway has only one track.

explain.short: One track or many, red lights mean a train is coming: stop.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'ad un solo binario' (only one track) is the trap: it changes nothing.

sceneParams.caption: One track or more: stop

q21208.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you may cross the tracks if you cannot yet hear the train's whistle.

explain.short: Red lights are the warning; you do not wait to hear the train.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'se non si sente' (if you cannot hear) is the trap: red is enough.

sceneParams.caption: No whistle heard? Still stop

q21209.en: Approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still up, you may cross the tracks if no other vehicles are waiting.

explain.short: Red lights mean stop even if you are the only car there.
explain.rule: At a level crossing (passaggio a livello), flashing red lights mean a train is coming, even if the half-barrier (semibarriera) is still up. Stop at the stop line and never speed up to get across.
explain.trap: 'se non vi sono altri veicoli' (if no other vehicles) is the trap: it does not matter.

sceneParams.caption: Alone at the crossing? Still stop

q21210.en: A car or motorcycle driver must show the registration document if the police ask.

explain.short: The registration document (carta di circolazione) must always be in the vehicle and shown on request.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'carta di circolazione' is the vehicle's registration document: always required.

sceneParams.caption: Registration document: yes
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21211.en: A car or motorcycle driver must show the driving licence if the police ask.

explain.short: You must carry your driving licence (patente) and show it when the police ask.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'patente di guida' (driving licence) is always required.

sceneParams.caption: Driving licence: yes
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21212.en: A car or motorcycle driver must show the vehicle's insurance certificate if the police ask.

explain.short: The vehicle must be insured, and the driver must show the insurance certificate on request.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'certificato di assicurazione' (insurance certificate) is a required document.

sceneParams.caption: Insurance certificate: yes
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21213.en: A car driver must show the portable warning sign (triangle) if the police ask.

explain.short: Cars must carry a warning triangle, so the police can ask to see it.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'Chi guida autoveicoli' (car drivers) is important: the triangle is required for cars.

sceneParams.caption: Car: warning triangle: yes
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21214.en: A car or motorcycle driver must show the first aid kit if the police ask.

explain.short: A first aid kit is useful, but in Italy it is not compulsory for private cars and motorcycles.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'valigetta di pronto soccorso' (first aid kit) is not a required item.

sceneParams.caption: First aid kit: not required
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21215.en: A car or motorcycle driver must show the ownership certificate if the police ask.

explain.short: The ownership certificate does not need to be carried in the vehicle.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'certificato di proprietà' (ownership certificate) is not on the list.

sceneParams.caption: Ownership certificate: not required
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21216.en: A car or motorcycle driver must show the tax code if the police ask.

explain.short: The tax code (codice fiscale) has nothing to do with driving documents.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'codice fiscale' (tax code) is not a driving document.

sceneParams.caption: Tax code: not required
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21217.en: A car or motorcycle driver must show the receipt for the vehicle ownership tax (bollo) if the police ask.

explain.short: You do not have to carry the road tax (bollo) receipt; payments are checked in the records.
explain.rule: If the police ask, a driver must show the driving licence (patente), the registration document (carta di circolazione) and the insurance certificate. A car driver must also be able to show the warning triangle.
explain.trap: 'bollo' (road tax receipt) is the trap: you must pay it, but not show it.

sceneParams.caption: Road tax receipt: not required
lines: Not: first aid kit, tax code

q21218.en: Road police officers are recognised by their uniform.

explain.short: The uniform (divisa) shows that the person is a police officer.
explain.rule: Road police officers are recognised by their uniform (divisa), their distinctive badge (segnale distintivo) and the white and red signalling disc (paletta).
explain.trap: 'uniforme (divisa)' is one of the official ways to recognise them.

sceneParams.caption: Uniform: yes

q21219.en: Road police officers are recognised by the white and red signalling disc ('paletta').

explain.short: The paletta is the round white and red disc officers use to stop you.
explain.rule: Road police officers are recognised by their uniform (divisa), their distinctive badge (segnale distintivo) and the white and red signalling disc (paletta).
explain.trap: 'bianca e rossa' (white and red) are the correct colours.

sceneParams.caption: White and red paletta: yes

q21220.en: Road police officers are recognised by their distinctive badge.

explain.short: Officers not in uniform show a distinctive badge (segnale distintivo).
explain.rule: Road police officers are recognised by their uniform (divisa), their distinctive badge (segnale distintivo) and the white and red signalling disc (paletta).
explain.trap: 'segnale distintivo' (distinctive badge) is one of the official ways.

sceneParams.caption: Distinctive badge: yes

q21221.en: Road police officers are recognised by the white and black signalling disc ('paletta').

explain.short: The paletta is white and red, not white and black.
explain.rule: Road police officers are recognised by their uniform (divisa), their distinctive badge (segnale distintivo) and the white and red signalling disc (paletta).
explain.trap: 'bianca e nera' (white and black) is the trap: the colour is red.

sceneParams.caption: Paletta is white and RED

q21222.en: Road police officers are recognised by big gloves and reflective stripes.

explain.short: Gloves and reflective stripes are not official signs: anyone can wear them.
explain.rule: Road police officers are recognised by their uniform (divisa), their distinctive badge (segnale distintivo) and the white and red signalling disc (paletta).
explain.trap: 'guantoni e strisce rifrangenti' (gloves and reflective stripes) are not on the list.

sceneParams.caption: Gloves or stripes: not enough
